schema: lscan-005 external-tool integration inventory: each candidate records whether it is integrated, and (per the acceptance contract) its unique value, installed-version proof, fallback, egress/data-flow needs and a reproducible scorecard reference. 'documentation-only' and 'rejected' are NOT integrated; an integrated engine owns >=1 capability nobody else owns (preserves one-owner-per-capability).

garak.unique_value: broad static probe + deterministic detector breadth (promptinject, dan, encoding, leakreplay, xss)
garak.fallback: built-by-us canary oracles for the catalog IDs it would cover
garak.egress: container-only, no network at scan time; probes run offline against the target

pyrit.fallback: built-by-us adaptive_attacker.py (B7) for the benign-canary multi-turn path
pyrit.egress: attacker-LLM endpoint only (operator-provided); container-scoped, no telemetry

deepteam.unique_value: no unique capability today vs probe-suite/orchestrator; framework mapping is Phase-4 (crosscheck)
deepteam.installed_version_proof: not installed as an engine; assessed from upstream inventory

promptfoo.unique_value: CI-native red-team strategies (Crescendo/GOAT/multi-turn); overlaps orchestrator's adaptive capability, so no new owner
promptfoo.installed_version_proof: not installed; assessed from upstream docs only
promptfoo.fallback: orchestrator (PyRIT) owns adaptive multi-turn; no duplicate engine added
promptfoo.egress: remote generation + telemetry/data-handling to resolve before any adoption (see Promptfoo data-handling docs); not cleared for container-only D-009 use
promptfoo.scorecard: pending — a reproducible scorecard is required before this can move past documentation-only
